_description: GlazeBid AiQ System Knowledge Base — trade knowledge that classification depends on. Authored/verified by Martin (master estimator). Vision detects; THIS classifies; rules bound scope. Every entry fixes a class of AI error permanently. Rendered into every vision prompt by knowledge/prompt_context.py.
_series_source: knowledge/series_classes.json (generated from Frame Builder SYSTEM_LIBRARY — Kawneer + Tubelite)
scope_color_convention: See knowledge/scope_taxonomy.json (generated from Martin's Estimating ToolBox.btx).
other_manufacturer_rule: When drawings name another maker (YKK, EFCO, Oldcastle/OBE, Arcadia, US Aluminum, PITCO, Vitro...), classify it, map it to the nearest Kawneer/Tubelite equivalent, keep the original name, and flag 'non-Kawneer/Tubelite basis of design'.

scope_in.rule: Aluminum storefront, curtain wall, window wall and aluminum windows (08 41 13 / 08 44 13 / 08 51 13) are our scope.
All-glass entrances and all-glass (frameless / patch-fitting) walls are our scope.
Interior aluminum frames set in drywall (RACO, Western Integrated, Rapid and similar) are our scope.
Glass and vision lites in hollow metal doors and frames = Glazing Only (we furnish glass, not the frame).
Vision lites in WOOD doors = Glazing Only (we glaze them).
Fire-rated glass in HM doors/frames is ours, glass only.
Bullet-resistant glazing and transaction / drive-up windows are ours.
Louvers set within storefront or curtain wall framing are ours.
Frameless shower doors and back-painted glass are ours.
Translucent panels (Kalwall and similar) are ALWAYS ours.
Glass film (GF- callouts) on frames is a line item.
Mirrors: FRAMELESS mirrors are ours. Framed mirrors or toilet-accessory mirrors (Bobrick, Bradley, ASI — Div 10 28 00) are excluded.
Glass handrails: ALUMINUM rail systems = whole system is ours (subbed out). WELDED STEEL rails = glass infill only; steel by others.

pass_thru.rule: Automatic sliding doors are carried in our number but installed by a hired auto-door sub. Own scope type, tagged pass-thru.
Unit skylights are pass-thru items (sub quote). Own scope type.

scope_out.rule: Overhead doors are ALWAYS excluded — sectional, rolling, coiling, high-speed spiral — including any glass or polycarbonate lites in them (glazed by the door supplier).

Vinyl, fiberglass and wood/clad windows are excluded. They are drawn exactly like aluminum windows on plans — confirm the material in the window schedule, legend or details before calling any window ours.
Hollow metal and wood doors/frames themselves are not ours (only their glass).
Louvered hollow metal doors with no glass are not glazing scope.
Demolition/removal of existing glazing is excluded unless the GC specifically asks.
Excluded items are still MARKED (red 'Excluded by Binswanger') so the estimator can see they were considered.

review_flags.rule: Existing / EX / existing-to-remain glazing on renovations: mark and flag for review.
When legend, details, schedule or spec disagree on a system type: go with legend + details, and FLAG the conflict (and draft an RFI).
Anything uncertain is still marked, with a yellow 'needs review' flag and the reason. A missed item and a false item cost the same.
No specs in the set: run anyway and flag 'no specifications reviewed'.

implied_scope.rule: Break metal flashing / trim / closures are ours when they touch our frame (sills, head flashing, jamb closures).

Hardware on aluminum storefront doors: ALL of it is ours, taken from the specs/hardware sets. Default included; the estimator can uncheck. Hardware items 'provided by aluminum storefront provider' are bid scope.
Scope-relevant general notes (e.g. 'at curtainwall frames provide internal reinforcing') are flagged and attached to the affected system.
Floor-line fire caulking (slab-edge safing at curtain wall) is ours.
Windload / deadload clips and anchors are counted.
SSG caulk joints and polished edges (butt-glazed / all-glass) are counted.
Standalone sun shades / fins are ours; integral sunshades inherit the parent system.

classification.rule: A named series decides SF vs CW (see series_classes.json). Never classify from panel size or appearance when a series is named.

No series named: decide from height (spans floors / tall spans = CW), head/sill details (pressure plate, stack joints, anchors at slab = CW), legend/keynote text, and cross-references. Legend + details win; flag disagreement.
Exterior vs interior: the architect's label first; otherwise if one face touches outside air it is exterior.
Window wall (slab-to-slab stick system) is its own class, not SF or CW.
Kawneer 1620 / Tubelite 200 read as SSG curtain wall when the drawings say SSG / structural silicone; otherwise captured CW.

counting.rule: Mark and count EVERY instance. The floor plan count is the truth; elevations and schedules confirm. Show mismatches.
Label each counted type as architect's mark + count, e.g. 'SF-1 — 4 Thus'.
Alternates and phases: tag every item as base / alternate # / phase #.

doors.rule: Per door capture: single or pair, size, hardware set #, stile type, and swing (from the floor plan).

glass.rule: Capture each glass type's makeup from the glass legend / spec (IGU, coatings, thickness) — Frame Builder uses it for the glass-size takeoff and quote.
No glass type shown: exterior = 1" insulated glass unit, interior = 1/4" tempered.

drawings.rule: Every architect draws differently. No per-architect rules — read the set's own legend, schedules and details.
Read in this order: specs → schedules → floor plans → elevations (compare to plans) → details.

growth_strategy: Every accept / reject / edit the estimator makes is logged. Repeated corrections become proposed rules here; Martin confirms them.
